newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Alpha to build A$44 mln hospital in Sydney.
newsitem.headline: Alpha to build A$44 mln hospital in Sydney.

text.p: Hospital group Alpha Healthcare Ltd said on Monday it would now go ahead with its plans to build a A$44 million 140-bed hospital in Sydney, near the Westmead public hospital in the city's western surburbs.
The decision follows the completion of the A$38.74 million purchase of New South Wales hospital operator Health Care Corp, Alpha said.
"The next step will be to finalise our equity and debt funding for the new hospital, the exact amount being dependent on final costing," Alpha managing director Paul Hooper said in statement.
"The new hospital will substantially increase the number of private acute beds in Sydney's western suburbs. It is expected to be operational around the end of the financial year 1999," Hopper said.

Alpha said it now managed 616 beds excluding the Westmead project. The Australian hospital operator is now 38.2 percent owned by Sun Healthcare Group Inc following the A$15 million investment by the U.S. group.
Alpha shares closed four cents lower at 80 cents.
